Singapore Logistics Resilience Monitor

Leading indicators for Singapore's logistics sector from public data, with alarms backtested against 8 documented disruptions (2020–2026). Code, sources and method: GitHub repository.

Level 3: Activate review

As of 2026-10-11 (PortWatch data to 2026-10-04; MPA to 2026-08; Changi to 2026-08; GSCPI to 2026-09).
Last known alarms: Bab el-Mandeb transits, Singapore container-ship port calls, Singapore TEU per container-ship call, NY Fed Global Supply Chain Pressure Index.
Unavailable detector input at the latest published slot: Singapore container-ship port calls, Singapore container trade volume (estimate), Port Klang container-ship port calls, Tanjung Pelepas container-ship port calls. An unavailable input retains an existing alarm; it does not confirm current stress or recovery.

Alert level over time

Watch: any indicator in alarm. Alert: two route indicators, or a route indicator plus a Singapore or regional one. Activate review: Alert plus a Singapore monthly outcome in alarm. Each day uses only data that had been published by then. Missing observations reset consecutive confirmation and recovery counts while retaining the last known alarm; hover to see unavailable inputs. Grey bands are the labelled events.

Shipping routes (IMF PortWatch)

Singapore and global pressure

TEU per call = MPA container throughput divided by PortWatch container-ship calls. Container throughput and air cargo are plotted as year-on-year log change x100 (close to % change), the form the detector uses.

Backtest: first alarm per event and indicator

Selected setting (tuned on 2020–2022 only): z ≥ 2.5, 3 consecutive days. "known" = the day the alarm could have been read, including the source's publication lag. Lag is counted from the documented onset.
